minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted a two-year extension to rebuild a fire-damaged house at 135 Highland Street; motion carried by voice vote.
minutes.summary: The board heard a petition from the owner of 135 Highland Street for more time to finish rebuilding a non-conforming house destroyed by fire, after the two-year window expired in October 2024. The building official clarified it was an extension of the reconstruction time period, not of a special permit. A neighbor and a local pastor spoke in support, and the board voted to grant a two-year extension and then adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to grant a two-year extension of the time to rebuild a fire-damaged house at 135 Highland Street; it passed by voice vote.
The building official said the request extends the reconstruction time period, not a special permit; the original two-year window had expired in October 2024.
A neighbor and a local pastor spoke in support of the owner's petition during public comment.
The chair read the post-decision conditions, including filing with the town clerk within 14 days and recording at the registry of deeds before the decision takes effect.

why_it_matters: This touches one household and one street: the owner of a non-conforming house destroyed by fire keeps the right to rebuild after the original window lapsed.
The decision does not take effect until it is recorded at the registry of deeds, so the extension is not final on the day of the vote.
